_about: Reusable scene shapes for Paper Cinema Shorts. Procedure and taste rules: .claude/skills/scene-writing/SKILL.md; human guide: docs/SCENE-WRITING.md. Each beat: pct = [from, to] as % of the scene body (the 6 s signature opening comes before it, the 2.6 s end card overlays its end); purpose; lines = line ideas (rewrite them, never paste them as-is); moves = names from library/moves.json or library/poses.json (checked); shot = a shot type shared with library/shots.json (eye-reveal, blade-slide, low-hero-push, whip-reveal, orbit-zanshin, silhouette-wide, over-shoulder-standoff, impact-zoom); sound = ids in assets/sfx/ or a description for a new query; effect = what to show, with 'planned' where the engine cannot do it yet. jhk = jo / ha / kyu / zanshin phase (or ki / sho / ten / ketsu for kishotenketsu-shaped templates).

templates.name: Standoff and single cut
templates.useWhen: Two fighters, one decision. The classic samurai-film ending: a long stillness, one flash, the loser's light goes out late.
templates.voice: Optional. A witness narrator works best; 3-5 lines; nothing in the 2 s before the cut.
templates.references: Sanjuro's final duel (about 20 s of stillness, one flash) [C]; Strike Grammar.

beats.purpose: Hook: the stake in one image and one line
lines: Name the cost: 'Only one of them was getting back in the boat.'

beats.purpose: Distance: show the space between them and what each wants
lines: One concrete detail about each fighter's weapon or habit (the set-up)

beats.purpose: Pressure: a step, a shift of grip, a line that cuts deeper than steel
lines: The provocation or the quiet verdict

beats.purpose: Ma: nothing moves; one eye
beats.effect: eye glow brightest thing on screen

beats.purpose: The cut: once, frozen in hit-stop
beats.sound: whoosh-b, impact, paper tear, wet splat 0.1 s later

beats.purpose: Delayed result: the loser's paper splits or the light fades; the victor holds
lines: One short line of aftermath, a noun at the end

pitfalls: A clash before the cut kills the stillness
Showing the cut at normal speed in a wide
Music over the ma

templates.name: Monologue before battle
templates.useWhen: The owner's reference format: one character, 15-25 s of voice, slow dark heroic shots, one gesture.
templates.voice: 4-6 lines, 3-12 words each, pauses 0.8-2.5 s, lines shorten toward the gesture; one triad at most.
templates.references: research/reference-videos.md (videos A and C); Henry V for anaphora and the triad [C].

beats.purpose: Hook: the eye and the first line, a personal concrete image
lines: 'My mother folded this armour from her prayers.'
beats.effect: 70% darkness; glow pulses with stressed words (planned)

beats.purpose: Memory: what this person carries (the set-up)
lines: A count, a habit, a place: 'One for every winter I came home.'

beats.purpose: The admission: the stake, said sideways (subtext)
lines: 'There are not enough for today.'

beats.purpose: The one gesture: sword raised into the single shaft of light
lines: The resolve, rising: 'So I will spend them slowly.'

beats.purpose: Scale and loss: small figure in the dark or fog, the last line, cut to black
lines: An order or a gift, ending on a noun: 'look for the light.'
beats.sound: music swells under the last line, then dead silence
beats.effect: glow dims one step; fog (planned); end card

pitfalls: Speeches about honour or destiny
More than one gesture
Fast cutting; the voice drives the rhythm

templates.name: Cursed blade awakens
templates.useWhen: Fiction thread: a cursed sword (library/swords) shows its hunger; the wielder chooses. The Ronin never speaks; the blade may whisper (our choice).
templates.voice: Another character states the legend as a threat; the sword gets 2-6 whispered words; the wielder says nothing.
templates.references: docs/STORY-BIBLE.md (Kurenai-oni cuts the light out of whatever it touches).

beats.purpose: Hook: the legend as a stake
lines: 'Every man who carried that sword is dead.'
beats.effect: crimson leaks at the seam of the scabbard

beats.purpose: The sword as a character: its want
lines: Whisper, delighted: 'She is so bright.'

beats.purpose: The flicker: amber eyes go crimson for 2 frames
lines: The other character pleads in one word

beats.purpose: Ma before the draw
The draw-cut: what he cuts is the choice (the pay-off)
beats.effect: crimson smear ribbon, ink impact frame, light of the cut object goes out

beats.purpose: Cost: the eyes return to amber slowly, or do not
lines: The sword, sulking: '...Next time.'

pitfalls: Explaining the colour code
A demonic voice with heavy effects; keep the whisper human and close
Letting the Ronin talk

templates.name: Duel in the rain
templates.useWhen: An exchange of 2-4 moves where weather is the obstacle and the clock: footing, sight, the paper getting wet. Only if the rain means something.
templates.voice: Little or none. Rain is the score; footsteps and clashes on its rhythm (Zatoichi 2003 lesson [C]).
templates.references: research/anime-fight-craft.md sound section; Strike Grammar exchange.

beats.purpose: Hook: a drop hits a blade edge and runs off as paint-red light
lines: Optional: 'The paper was already soaking.'
beats.sound: rain on paper (new query: 'rain on roof light')
beats.effect: rain (planned); wet darkening of washi (SHIMI, planned on 3D)

beats.purpose: Distance and footing: who is standing where, and what water does to paper
Exchange, getting faster: attack, block, attack, dodge
beats.sound: clash-steel, clash-light, steel-scrape on the rain rhythm

beats.purpose: The slip or the bind: the weather decides
beats.sound: rain drops out to near silence

beats.purpose: The cut
The rain keeps falling; it washes the paint
lines: One line, or the rain alone

pitfalls: Rain as decoration
A clash every second with no rhythm
Too long an exchange in a 45 s Short

templates.name: Master and student
templates.useWhen: A lesson told as a duel or a correction: the master wins without cutting. Kishotenketsu shape: the twist is what the lesson really was.
templates.voice: Dialogue, 4-6 lines total; the master speaks least; the last line is the student's, or silence.

beats.purpose: Hook: the student attacks the master at full speed
lines: Student: 'Again.'

beats.purpose: Development: every attack fails the same way
lines: Master, one correction, concrete: 'Your feet arrive before your sword.'

beats.purpose: Twist: the master lowers the sword; the lesson was not about the cut
lines: Master: 'Now. Don't.'

beats.purpose: The student stops a cut a finger from the master's throat (the pay-off)
beats.sound: whoosh-b cut off dead, no impact
beats.effect: hit-stop with no contact; impact frame without shards

beats.purpose: Reconciliation: both glows calm to the same amber
lines: Student, quietly, the lesson in a noun

pitfalls: The master giving a speech
Stating the moral
Making the student look stupid instead of eager

templates.name: The last stand
templates.useWhen: One against many, or one holding a place: the stake is time, not victory. Ends in a light going out, or in dawn.
templates.voice: A short monologue (3-4 lines) before the stand, nothing during it, one line or none after.
templates.references: Story bible episode 4 (the Gold Armoured Samurai at Sekigahara); battle-speech rhythm (anaphora) [C].

beats.purpose: Hook: what is being protected, in one image
lines: 'They need until dawn. The bridge is narrow.'

beats.purpose: The odds: silhouettes of many; the one
lines: A count: 'Twelve on the bridge. One of me. One bridge.'

beats.purpose: The stand: exchanges, each costing light
beats.effect: his glow dims a step after each exchange

beats.purpose: The last cut, given everything
beats.effect: biggest shard burst of the episode

beats.purpose: He stays standing as his light goes out; the sky lightens behind
lines: None, or the first line returned (the loop)
beats.effect: light goes out; dawn rises; end card

pitfalls: Killing faceless enemies for spectacle (no cruelty, story bible)
Too many exchanges in a Short
A triumphant ending that betrays the loss

templates.name: Iaido draw
templates.useWhen: A single draw-cut from the scabbard as the whole scene: the weapon is the character. Good for sword introductions and episode teasers.
templates.voice: None or one line before the draw. The sound of the draw is the line.
templates.references: Iaido sequence: draw, cut, chiburi (flick the blade clean), noto (re-sheathe) [C] (research/anime-fight-craft.md 1d).

beats.purpose: Hook: the hand rests on the hilt; the seam glows
lines: Optional: the sword's name and one fact of its legend

beats.purpose: Waiting: breathing, the target (a falling leaf, a candle, a paper crane)
The draw-cut, faster than the eye; hide it
Delayed result: the target falls in two a beat later
Chiburi and noto: paint flicked off, blade home with a hard click
lines: One line after the click, or none
beats.sound: flick whoosh, hard wooden click with no reverb
beats.effect: paint flick (chiburi pose planned); end card

pitfalls: Showing the draw clearly at normal speed
No delayed result
A reverb tail on the sheathe click (it must feel final)

templates.name: Aftermath (zanshin)
templates.useWhen: The fight already happened (events with negative times). The scene is what remains: mono no aware, the pathos of things passing.
templates.voice: One survivor or witness, 3-5 lines, slow, tired; the lines are about objects, not feelings.
templates.references: Mono no aware and sabi (SEP Japanese Aesthetics) [D]; Harakiri's out-of-order telling [C].

beats.purpose: Hook: the result first, a fallen light or a broken blade
lines: 'It was over before the gulls came back.'
beats.effect: one light out, one still on

beats.purpose: Objects: what the fight left (a scabbard in the surf, a headband tail)
lines: Three objects, one per line (the one triad)
beats.effect: paint drying on paper (SHIMI tide line)

beats.purpose: Ink-world flash: the moment, in sumi-e memory (1-2 s)
beats.effect: ink world black-and-white (story bible rule 4); grade planned

beats.purpose: The survivor turns away; the gesture of leaving
lines: The shortest line: what he did next

beats.purpose: The place without them; the sea returns (the loop)
lines: A last object kept: 'I kept the shavings.'
beats.effect: crane up (KUROKO crane feel); end card

pitfalls: Grief stated aloud
Lingering on the dead body (show the light going out instead)
Too many flashbacks; one ink flash is enough

templates.name: The witness
templates.useWhen: A historical duel told by a minor or fictional onlooker (boatman, retainer, child, the sea). The honest way to voice history: our words in a witness's mouth, tradition labelled.
templates.voice: The witness narrates in past tense, 5-8 lines; the historical figure speaks only a traditional line, labelled.
templates.references: research/ganryujima.md; worked example A in the scene-writing skill.

beats.purpose: Hook: the witness's relation to the hero, one line
lines: 'I rowed him to the island. He did not speak once.'

beats.purpose: The detail only the witness saw (the set-up)
lines: 'He carved my spare oar into a sword.' (tradition, labelled)

beats.purpose: The other side: the opponent waiting, the gesture that loses (scabbard thrown)
lines: The traditional line, by the hero, cold: 'You have already lost.'

beats.purpose: Ma
The blow
What the witness kept
lines: 'One blow. Then he asked me to row.'
'I kept the shavings.'

pitfalls: Captioning invented lines as the historical figure's quote
The witness explaining the hero's psychology
Unlabelled tradition
